section_summary: This closing section completes a statistical report on Japanese armaments production in 1942, including privately owned Matsukata-Jugo Ginko interests and an overall government/private production summary. It then contains a 1943 telegram record, a pair of April 1941 letters concerning a telegram to Yokohama, a badly degraded fragment about forces or aircraft in the Far East, and a 1944 cross-reference concerning Swedish shipments, an oil refinery, and bearings sought from SKF.

subfiles.title: Tables XIV–XV: Japanese Armaments Production in 1942
subfiles.about: Tables summarize 1942 weapons production by Matsukata-Jugo Ginko interests and by Japanese government-controlled and privately owned plants.
subfiles.summary: Table XIV records monthly output of rifles, automatic weapons, small-caliber cannon, antiaircraft guns, and shells at privately owned plants associated with Matsukata-Jugo Ginko. Notes identify Tokyo Gas & Electricity Works as the main plant, describe plant conversions and amalgamations, and give a labor force of 17,960. Table XV consolidates monthly armaments production and inventories for government-controlled and private plants, covering firearms, artillery, ammunition, tanks, bombs, mines, and explosives.

subfiles.title: Telegram Record from Charles K. Clark
subfiles.about: A telegram record identifies a communication sent from San Francisco by Charles K. Clark to the Secretary of State.
subfiles.summary: The page records San Francisco as the place of origin and June 4, 1943, as the transmission date. It identifies Charles K. Clark as sender and the Secretary of State as recipient, but no substantive message text survives on the page; filing stamps indicate receipt or processing on June 18, 1943.

subfiles.title: Letter from P. W. Parker to Stanley K. Hornbeck
subfiles.about: Parker reports agreement to send a telegram to Yokohama in its originally drafted form.
subfiles.summary: Parker tells Hornbeck that, following a further discussion with Wilkinson, the telegram to Yokohama will be sent in the form previously read by telephone and quoted in Walden's letter. Wilkinson will cable London with Parker's explanation of why the original wording was retained. Parker expresses satisfaction that Hornbeck's views have been accepted for the moment.

subfiles.title: Reply from Stanley K. Hornbeck to P. W. Parker
subfiles.about: Hornbeck acknowledges Parker's letter confirming the agreed wording of the Yokohama telegram.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck thanks Parker for his April 16 letter. He restates that, after the discussion with Wilkinson, the telegram to Yokohama will be sent in the form read to Hornbeck's office by telephone and reproduced in Walden's letter.

subfiles.title: Illegible Fragment Concerning Forces and Aircraft in the Far East
subfiles.about: A severely degraded fragment appears to refer to forces, particularly aircraft, in the Far East.
subfiles.summary: Only a few words can be recovered reliably from this page, including an apparent reference to forces, especially planes, in the Far East. The document's author, recipient, date, and larger argument cannot be determined from the surviving OCR.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Note on Swedish Shipments and Japanese Equipment Needs
subfiles.about: The sheet cross-references a document about an oil refinery, Sweden–Japan shipments, and bearings sought by Japan from SKF.
subfiles.summary: The cross-reference concerns equipment and supplies in Japan, the erection of a natural-oil refinery, and shipments between Sweden and Japan. It also mentions bearings desired by the Japanese from SKF. The original paper is dated October 28, 1944, and is filed under number 740.0011 E.W./10-2844.
